text: A fair 6-sided dice with faces labelled 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 is thrown repeatedly. The random variable X
denotes the number of throws required to obtain a 6.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Find the numerical value of Var(X ).

Find the probability that a score of 2 is obtained fewer than 8 times.

parts.text: Find the probability that the two discs that Priti chooses are blue.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Find the probability that the two discs that Priti chooses come from bag X given that at least one of
the discs is red.

text: Priti has two bags of discs, X and Y.
Bag X contains 8 red discs and 7 blue discs.
Bag Y contains 6 red discs and 9 blue discs.
Priti tosses a fair coin.
If she obtains a head, she chooses at random and without replacement two discs from bag X.
If she obtains a tail, she chooses at random and with replacement two discs from bag Y.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Draw a back-to-back stem-and-leaf diagram to represent the heights of the players from Pelicans
and Swans, with Pelicans on the left-hand side. 
* 0000800000009 * DFD

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Find the median and the interquartile range of the heights of the Pelicans. 
For the Swans, the lower quartile of the heights is 165 cm, the median is 174 cm and the upper quartile
is 181 cm.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Represent the data shown in the back-to-back stem-and-leaf diagram by a pair of box-and-whisker
plots in a single diagram.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Make one comparison between the heights of the Pelicans players and the heights of the
Swans players. 
* 0000800000010 * DFD

text: The heights, in cm, of 15 players from each of two sports teams, Pelicans and Swans, are given in
the table.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Find the number of different ways in which a team of 6 athletes can be selected if it consists of at
least 3 sprinters, at most 2 hurdlers and at most 1 thrower. 
* 0000800000011 * DFD
A group of 8 athletes chosen from the group of 25 athletes consists of 1 sprinter, 3 hurdlers and 4
throwers. These 8 athletes stand in a row.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
How many different arrangements of the 8 athletes are there if the 3 hurdlers do not stand all
together?

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
How many different arrangements of the 8 athletes are there in which there are at least two athletes
between any two hurdlers? 
* 0000800000012 * DFD

text: In a group of 25 athletes, there are 8 sprinters, 5 hurdlers and 12 throwers.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Find the probability that a randomly chosen runner took more than 55.1 seconds to complete
the run. 
In the second run, the times to complete the run were normally distributed with mean 39.8 seconds and
standard deviation v seconds. 10% of the runners took more than 48.6 seconds.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Find the value of v. 
* 0000800000013 * DFD
150 runners are chosen at random from those who took part in the second run.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Use an approximation to find the probability that fewer than 20 of the 150 runners took more than
48.6 seconds to complete the run.

text: A large number of runners took part in two charity runs to raise money for a new community centre.
In the first run, the times to complete the run were normally distributed with mean 46.3 seconds and
standard deviation 6.4 seconds.
